subject: in-memory sqlite database lost between connections
what: cd3_exporter opened a new sqlite3 connection per call, so :memory: gave every call its own empty database and the exporter's self-test failed on a table it had just created.
evidence: before: 'Export error: no such table: otel_spans', rc=1, 0 spans; after: cd3_exporter self-test rc=0, 2 spans ['self_test_root','child_span']
remedy: hold ONE connection for the lifetime of the database (_connect()/_release()), released by shutdown(); self-test reads through that same connection

subject: spawned repo hooks inherit the caller's cwd
what: tests/test_bible_ship.py spawned the real .githooks/pre-push with no cwd=, and a child process inherits the parent's working directory. The test's temp dir is nested inside a checkout (C:/Users/clint is itself a git repo), so the hook ran THAT repo's gates: 92 s for pre-push, 197 s for all three, and the suite read as a hang.
evidence: after: tests/test_bible_ship.py -> 16 passed in 1.24 s; negative controls fire (a doubled brace is rejected; a bare ${} form -> 'bad substitution')
remedy: cwd=tmp_path + git init -q so the hook sees an empty repo; token-level expansion via _expansions() keeps the coverage the guard skip removed. Class covered by scanner rule hook_spawn_without_cwd added 2026-11-04 (0 hits in src/ and tests/, positive and negative controls fire)
note: tests/test_bible_ship.py -> 16 passed in 1.24 s; b4f92756; scanner rule hook_spawn_without_cwd now covers the class

subject: token expansion probe was vacuous

note: per-token script probe replaces the shared eval; b4f92756

subject: exit status read from the pipeline tail, not the tested command
what: A probe printed rc=0 for a command argparse had REJECTED, because $? read tail's status: the scanner's 'error: unrecognized arguments' appeared next to rc=0. A filter that hides the tested command's status reports a failure as a pass.
evidence: output pairing 'scanner.py: error: unrecognized arguments' with 'rc=0'; re-run without the pipe: --list-rules -> '[WARNING] hook_spawn_without_cwd', 'Total: 21 rules'
remedy: no pipe when the exit status is the evidence; set -o pipefail or read the first element of PIPESTATUS
note: re-ran the bare command and read its own status; pipe removed

subject: two files fail only under the suite's own concurrency
what: The 2026-11-04 full run (exit=1) failed tests/test_worm_smoke.py at 43.2 s and tests/test_preflight_all.py at 224.7 s (164 passed, 1 failed, 1 error). Both files pass when run alone, so the failure is not in either file's logic: it appears only when 16 workers run alongside them. Both spawn child processes and touch shared stores (sqlite telemetry, ports), so a worker's child waits on a resource another worker holds and the file times out.
evidence: full run: logs/golden_arrow.json generated 2026-11-04T14:13:58Z -> files 520, passed 518, failed 2, hung 0, exit=1; isolation: tests/test_worm_smoke.py -> '5 passed in 19.36s'; tests/test_preflight_all.py -> '165 passed in 110.99s'
remedy: needs a repro that names the colliding resource (which child, which lock) before any fix; a worker-count change would be a suppression, not a fix
note: load-induced, not file-local: each file is green alone (5 passed; 165 passed); needs a repro naming the colliding resource
